text: Given a mocked Cloud Marketplace transport returning a products payload, when ingrammicro_cloud_list_products(vendor="VA-888-104") is called, then the tool's JSON result contains mpn/name/vendor/serviceName/billingPeriods/prices for each product, unmodified from the mocked response.
Given the same mock, when mpn, name, and service_name are all supplied, then the outbound request's query string includes mpn, name, and serviceName (and omits any filter left None).
Given vendor is omitted, when the tool is called, then it returns {"error": {"code": "invalid_argument", ...}} and the mock transport records zero calls.

Given no X-IngramMicro-Cloud-* headers are sent (with or without the 4 Resellers headers present), when ingrammicro_cloud_list_products is called, then the tool returns {"error": {"code": "not_configured", ...}} naming the 5 missing headers, and the gateway does not reject the HTTP request with a 401.
Given only the 4 Resellers headers are sent (no Cloud headers), when any of the 24 existing tools is called, then behavior is unchanged from before this change.
Given only the 5 Cloud headers are sent (no Resellers headers), when the HTTP request reaches the middleware, then it is NOT rejected with 401 (today it would be).
evidence: Not implemented as written -- see docs/tickets/PRD-21597.md Self-test "Changed/unimplemented test cases" for the full rationale. Summary: the gateway's blanket 401 for the 4 Resellers headers was deliberately left unchanged (still required on every /mcp request); only the Cloud Products bundle's own presence/absence is optional, matching sibling ticket PRD-21595's already-reviewed-and-accepted precedent for the Cloud Subscriptions bundle (that review's finding #1 flagged the identical gap as a non-blocking suggestion, not a must-fix). No AC in this ticket's AC1-AC7 actually requires a Cloud-Products-only caller to bypass the Resellers gate -- AC4/AC5 only test the inverse (Cloud headers absent, with/without Resellers present). This ticket's real tenant (Ginko IT) already has Resellers credentials per PRD-21595's own doc, so this does not block the ticket's actual use case. Flagged for review/design to decide whether to formally drop or re-scope this test case.

text: Given the mocked transport returns 401/403/404/422/429/500/503 in turn, when list_products is called, then IngramCloudClient raises IngramMicroError and .to_envelope() matches the existing _classify table exactly.

Given two sequential fake requests carry two different Cloud credential tuples, when each runs through GatewayTokenMiddleware, then _gateway_cloud_creds_var.get() inside each matches only that request's own headers, and the var is None again after each completes.

Given a real Ingram Micro Cloud Marketplace account for Ginko IT (or any onboarded reseller) with vendor=VA-888-104, when ingrammicro_cloud_list_products is called against the real upstream, then live Microsoft 365 SKUs are returned with usable mpn/name values.
steps: Obtain real Cloud Marketplace credentials for an onboarded reseller (client id/secret, marketplace code, subscription key, and the reseller's actual API base URL)
Set the 5 X-IngramMicro-Cloud-* headers on an MCP initialize + tools/call request for ingrammicro_cloud_list_products
expect: HTTP 200 from the tool, no error envelope; response contains at least one product with a non-empty mpn and name recognizable as a Microsoft 365 SKU
evidence: Not run during this design/dev pass: no real Ingram Micro Cloud Marketplace account was available (per mcp-track.md, missing a real vendor account is not a blocker; this test case documents the gap rather than silently skipping it). Needs a real vendor account before this tool is relied on in production.
